notes: Independent live fee audit of all 14 records: 10 discovery journals and 4 diamond additions. Every record receives a full route replacement and per-record audit_note. No other role files were changed.

Conservative result: 6 verified_free, 7 needs_verification, and 1 conditional. The four Sage demotions record contradictory generic page-charge language; they do not assert that a page fee actually exists. Explicit known-free submission/publication fees remain recorded.

For Sage PPA, Evaluation, ARPA and PWMP, the explicit no-fee statement coexists with a statement that OA fees exclude separate page/colour charges. No official page-fee schedule, trigger or exemption was found. Normal length guidance was not invented as a contractual free-page exemption.

Administration & Society and Science, Technology, & Human Values have explicit no-submission/no-publication-fee statements without the separate page-charge warning in the inspected guide. ST&HV explicitly makes print colour free. Evaluation is online-only.

Policy Sciences and Science and Public Policy remain unconfirmed for submission fees; JEPP author instructions remain blocked. Cambridge Journal of Public Policy is wholly OA, with assessed funding/waiver routes. Its no-APC Letters exception does not establish a free full research article.

All four added diamond journals retain verified_free status based on explicit author-fee policies. Internet Policy Review's 2026 research screening delay, separate op-ed closure and full AI policy are retained.

No venue was contacted, no manuscript submitted, and no membership, account or paid service purchased. Review/metric/ranking fields and OSRI scope are unchanged; this audit is policy research rather than human scientific review.
